title: The Borrowed Alibi
premise: Estate lawyer Mara Ravensworth is hired to probate a will naming a woman, Elise Vann, who was declared legally dead seven years ago — and the will's execution date falls after her disappearance. When Mara locates Elise's diary and finds entries written years past the date she vanished, he realizes someone has been impersonating the dead woman to control her inheritance. As Mara traces the forged identity through a web of family trustees, he discovers his own firm helped bury the original case. To close it before the statute expires, Mara must expose the living impostor — Elise's brother-in-law, who faked her death to seize the estate — and in doing so forfeits the partnership he spent his career building, choosing justice over belonging.
about_author: Wendell Ravensworth is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families tear themselves apart over paper. He writes mysteries about the lies people notarize.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Mara Ravensworth, POV. A courier delivers a sealed will for probate naming Elise Vann — declared dead seven years ago — with an execution date two years after her disappearance. Mara's instinct says fraud; his pride says take the case. Emotional beat: cold curiosity sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ashworth House
chapters.summary: Mara visits the Vann estate, now managed by trustee Gregory Vann, Elise's brother-in-law, who is charming, cooperative, and subtly discouraging. The house feels staged, like a museum of a life. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional courtesy.

chapters.title: The Diary
chapters.summary: Mara tracks down Elise's personal effects in storage and finds her diary. The final entry is dated three years after she vanished. His hands shake reading it. Emotional beat: the case stops being abstract — someone alive wrote those words.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Mara pulls the original missing-person file and finds his own firm's fingerprints on the death declaration — his mentor, Aldous Crane, handled it. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ground under his career cracks.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Elise's estranged sister Nadia, POV. Nadia recalls the last year before Elise disappeared: Gregory's debts, Elise's plan to change the will, a fight nobody will confirm. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Mara learns the estate can be reopened only within ninety days of the fraudulent will surfacing — and someone filed it deliberately, knowing the deadline. The case has a fuse. Emotional beat: urgency replacing caution.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Mara decodes the diary's later entries: coded references to 'the boathouse' and 'the second key.' He visits the boathouse at night and finds a hidden compartment, empty but recently disturbed. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Gregory's Generosity
chapters.summary: Gregory offers Mara a lucrative retainer to drop the probate challenge, framed as protecting the family from scandal. Mara declines with a smile. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused — barely.

chapters.title: Crane's Confession
chapters.summary: Mara confronts his mentor. Aldous admits he signed the death paperwork under pressure but claims he never knew who pressured him — only that the instructions came with the firm's own letterhead. Emotional beat: shame shared across generations.

chapters.title: Nadia's Return
chapters.summary: Nadia arrives at Ashworth House uninvited, demanding answers, and Gregory has her removed by security. Mara witnesses the power he holds over the household staff — fear, not loyalty. Emotional beat: the mask slipping.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Mara matches the diary's cipher to a safe-deposit box at a shuttered bank branch. Inside: Elise's real will, naming Nadia as heir, dated one week before her disappearance. Emotional beat: triumph that immediately terrifies him — now he holds what someone killed for.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Someone runs Mara off the road on the way back from the bank. He survives; the box's contents are photographed copies, originals intact. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Staff Saw
chapters.summary: A former housekeeper, POV. She recounts the night Elise 'left': Gregory's car at the boathouse, a tarp, and a woman's coat burned in the incinerator. She stayed silent for seven years out of need for the job. Emotional beat: complicity and its long cost.

chapters.title: The Impostor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara traces Gregory's finances: the estate has been bled through shell companies since the death declaration. The inheritance wasn't the motive — it was the lifeline. Emotional beat: understanding corruption as desperation weaponized.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: With four days left on the statute, Mara files to reopen probate. Gregory's lawyers counter with an ethics complaint against Mara, freezing his practice license provisionally. Emotional beat: the system turning on him.

chapters.title: Alone at the Firm
chapters.summary: The partnership votes to distance itself from Mara. Aldous abstains — the closest thing to support he can offer. Mara packs his office, keeping only the diary. Emotional beat: exile; belonging traded for truth.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Revisited
chapters.summary: Acting on the housekeeper's account, police divers search the water near the boathouse and find a car matching Elise's — with no body inside. Gregory's alibi for that night collapses. Emotional beat: the past surfacing literally.

chapters.title: Where Is Elise Vann?
chapters.summary: Mara realizes the diary's final entries were written by someone with access to Elise's handwriting samples — Gregory practiced for months. But the last genuine entry suggests Elise planned to disappear herself, to escape him. Emotional beat: the victim reframed as an agent.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Ashworth
chapters.summary: Climax. Mara presents the evidence to Gregory in the estate's study, recording everything. Gregory breaks — first bluster, then confession: he staged the death, Elise fled rather than play along, and he's been writing the diary to keep the fiction alive. Police arrive mid-confession. Emotional beat: catharsis and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Living Will
chapters.summary: A letter arrives, postmarked abroad, from Elise herself — alive, having watched from hiding until it was safe. She authorizes Nadia as her representative. Emotional beat: relief so sharp it hurts.

chapters.title: Probate Closed
chapters.summary: The court voids the fraudulent will, restores the true one, and lifts Mara's provisional suspension. Aldous offers him his old office back. Mara asks instead for the firm's missing-persons archive. Emotional beat: quiet victory, changed priorities.

chapters.title: The Case Everyone Swore Was Closed
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mara's POV. Months later, Mara runs a small practice reopening dead cases. Elise sends a postcard with no return address — thanks enough. On his desk, a new file: another will that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: belonging found not in institutions, but in the work itself.
